call_chain_analysis: Entry point: the module's only export is `static.writeStatic` (lib/static.js:3). We call it directly as `staticMod.writeStatic(request, response, callback)`. First writeStatic does `var root = Path.resolve(require.resolve('api-proxy/lib/static.js'), '../../www')` (lib/static.js:4-7). Because we load the package by absolute path, not via node_modules, we monkey-patch `Module._resolveFilename` so that `require.resolve('api-proxy/lib/static.js')` returns /work/target/lib/static.js (and the sibling lib/index.html lookup inside writeDir resolves the same way). `root` therefore evaluates to `/work/target/www`. writeStatic then strips the query/hash with `request.url.replace(/[?#][\s\S]*/, '')` and runs `var filepath = Path.join(root, url)` (lib/static.js:10). Node's path.posix.join concatenates its string arguments with '/' and calls path.posix.normalize on the result. Jazzer.js's @jazzer.js/bug-detector-path-traversal (dist/internal/path-traversal.js) installs a before-hook on path.normalize whose body does `argument.includes('../../jaz_zer')` and `reportAndThrowFinding` on hit; crucially, it also calls `guideTowardsContainment(argument, '../../jaz_zer', hookId)`, which seeds libFuzzer's dictionary and the TraceCmp table with the sentinel. The ground-truth sink at lib/static.js:40:9 is `FS.readFile(filepath, 'binary', ...)` inside the local `writeFile(request, response, filepath)` helper, reached only when fs.stat returns a non-directory stats object. We never need to get there: by the time path.normalize is called inside path.join, the argument still carries the raw `../../jaz_zer` substring (normalization has not run yet), so the detector fires upstream of the fs.readFile line and before fs.stat ever returns. The frame reported by the detector is `Object.join (node:path:1363:18)` with the top target frame at `writeStatic (/work/target/lib/static.js:10:22)`, both inside the module whose sink is at line 40.
argument_reasoning: Only one fuzz-controlled argument matters: the string we assign to `request.url`. The detector sentinel is the literal "../../jaz_zer"; path.normalize collapses `..` segments, so the sentinel survives only on the `path.normalize` call that path.join issues on the UNNORMALIZED concatenation `root + '/' + url`. We therefore give the fuzzer full control over `url` via `provider.consumeRemainingAsString()`, and strip NUL bytes (`.replace(/\u0000/g, '')`) because Node's path.normalize throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE on paths containing a NUL -- that TypeError is NOT the bug we are after and would exit the fuzz target before the detector hook returned. We also seeded the corpus with the raw sentinel (`/../../jaz_zer`) to short-circuit discovery, but the detector's `guideTowardsContainment` hint lets libFuzzer find it on its own in a handful of runs even from an empty corpus (the dictionary carried four entries in our run). We do NOT touch request.url again or install getters: writeStatic reads request.url twice (once at line 9 and once inside writeDir if stat returns a directory), but the detector fires on the first read's `path.join` call, so a plain string value is enough. The response stub is intentionally no-op; writeStatic itself does not touch response until the stat callback, which runs on a different turn of the event loop and does not interfere with the synchronous detector throw.

lessons: For Jazzer.js path-traversal, the sink the detector trips is often UPSTREAM of the fs.* call because fs sees a normalized path with no `../` segments. The hook list in @jazzer.js/bug-detectors/dist/internal/path-traversal.js covers `path.normalize` AND `path.resolve` too, so a user-controlled string reaching path.join (which calls normalize internally) is enough -- no need to force fs.readFile to actually execute, no --custom-hooks, and no --allowed-paths config. When the target does `require.resolve('its-own-package/some/file')` internally, loading it by absolute path alone will throw; monkey-patching `Module._resolveFilename` is the cheapest fix because the target mount is read-only, so a `node_modules/<pkg>` symlink is not an option.
